name: Amateur-radio scholarships
deadline: The 2026 cycle is closed. The 2027 application dates have not been published.
apply: Complete the common online application with transcripts and any donor-required additional documents or club-officer recommendation.
eligibility: Active FCC-licensed amateur-radio operators pursuing higher education. Active foreign operators are eligible for ARDC awards. Each donor fund has its own geography, major and need conditions.

name: TCI Foundation Scholarship
deadline: Applications open January 1, 2027. The 2027 closing date has not been confirmed; the portal gives an undated annual March 31 closing date.
apply: Submit through a participating club or member-at-large in your state/province, with a 550-650-word essay, transcript, two recommendation letters and rating forms, and a photo. Club membership is not required.
eligibility: US or Canadian resident high school senior under 21, at least 6 feet 2 inches for men or 5 feet 10 inches for women in stocking feet; entering full-time accredited US/Canadian postsecondary education in the award calendar year.

name: Scholar-Chessplayer / Ambassador
deadline: The 2026 cycle is closed. The 2027 dates have not been published.
apply: Prior-cycle rules: apply online with transcripts, SAT/ACT scores, proof of 25 qualifying rated games, accomplishments and service, teacher and chess-coach recommendations, service-support letter, a 500-word essay and photo.
eligibility: Prior-cycle rules: current US Chess members who are high school juniors or seniors, with at least 25 qualifying regular-rated US Chess/FIDE games in the specified year and at least one year of service since grade 9. Ambassador applicants must be rated below 2000. Previous recipients are ineligible.

name: Anthem Essay Contest
value: Cash prizes; the current individual award schedule is not published.
deadline: The official contest dashboard says the entry deadline is coming soon.
apply: Select the contest, read the novel, create an account and submit original essays responding to the posted prompts.
eligibility: Middle and high school students worldwide, age 13 or older; enrolled in school during the contest.
notes: The official dashboard advertises up to $2,000 in prizes available for Anthem. This is not confirmed as the amount of one individual award.

name: The Fountainhead Essay Contest
deadline: The official contest dashboard says the entry deadline is coming soon.
apply: Select the contest, read the novel, create an account and submit original essays responding to the posted prompts.
eligibility: Middle and high school students worldwide, age 13 or older; enrolled in school during the contest.

name: Atlas Shrugged Essay Contest
deadline: The official contest dashboard says the entry deadline is coming soon.
apply: Select the contest, read the novel, create an account and submit original essays responding to the posted prompts.
eligibility: High school, college and graduate students worldwide, age 13 or older; enrolled in school during the contest.

name: MathWorks Math Modeling Challenge
value: Currently posted: $1,000-$20,000 per team; 2027 amounts unconfirmed
apply: Team of 3-5 plus coach.
eligibility: Prior-cycle rules: high school juniors or seniors at eligible US schools, or sixth-form students ages 16-19 at eligible schools in England or Wales. International/exchange students enrolled at eligible schools may enter. Homeschool/cyber students have separate age and documentation rules.
notes: Team scholarships are shared equally among 3-5 team members and paid to a college. Some specialty awards may be added. The published dollar schedule appears with 2026 rules; check the 2027 rules when released.

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium
value: Regional tuition awards: $1,000-$2,000; national oral awards: $4,000-$12,000; national poster cash awards: $350-$550
deadline: 2026-27 regional application deadlines vary; Arizona date TBD
apply: Apply through your regional Ideal-Logic registration with the abstract/research report and 2026-27 Statement of Outside Assistance. Regional selection precedes national competition.
eligibility: Students in grades 9-12 who are UScitizens or lawful permanent residents, including eligible American Samoa permanent residents, presenting original STEM research. One project and one regional competition per student; group research requires one designated presenter.
notes: National tuition awards are paid in four yearly installments after college enrollment and require 3.0 cumulative GPA and a STEM-related major; regional tuition awards are paid in the first college year. Other regional awards vary.

name: AFSA National High School Essay Contest
value: Previous first prize $2,500 plus educational travel
deadline: The 2025-2026 contest closed March 1, 2026. The 2027 prompt and deadline are not published.
apply: Prior-cycle rules: submit a 1,000-1,500-word original essay with MLA citations, at least three primary sources, and a teacher or sponsor. The top five essayists receive a short online interview. Check the next cycle rules before preparing an entry.
eligibility: Prior-cycle rules: grades 9-12 attending school in the 50 states, DC or US territories, or US citizens or lawful permanent residents attending high school overseas, including homeschool. Students whose parents are current or former Foreign Service members are excluded. Previous first-place winners and immediate family of AFSA, NSLC or Semester at Sea directors or staff are excluded.

name: DNA Day Essay Contest
deadline: The 2026 contest is closed. The 2027 prompt and application dates have not been published.
apply: Write an individual English essay of up to 750 words with references. A teacher or administrator submits it; a parent may submit for a homeschooled student.
eligibility: Grades 9-12 worldwide.

name: High School Essay Contest
deadline: February 21,2027, 11:59 p.m. CST (9:59 p.m. PST); topic and portal expected in December 2026
apply: Submit an original 300-500-word double-spaced essay as a Word file through JEA’s Submittable portal, with a $10 entry fee. Include a bibliography for external sources. AI-written work is disqualified.
eligibility: Grades 9-12 in US public, private or home schools. International student submissions and previous national winners are ineligible.

name: Teen Alzheimer's Awareness Scholarship
deadline: The 2026 award cycle is complete. The 2027 application dates have not been published.
apply: Prior-cycle rules: submit an essay of up to 1,500 words or a video of up to 4 minutes describing dementia impact, learning and future advocacy.
eligibility: Prior-cycle rules: current high school seniors living in the US who will attend a US college or university in fall; students already in college are ineligible. Entries describe Alzheimer’s/dementia impact, including family experience, research or advocacy.

name: Doodle for Google
apply: Prior-cycle rules: submit one original Google Doodle with the completed parent-signed entry form. AI-generated artwork is ineligible.
eligibility: Prior-cycle rules: K-12 students who are UScitizens or permanent legal residents at eligible US schools or homeschool, including DC, territories and freely associated states. Children of military personnel abroad may enter.

name: Stuck at Prom
value: Prior-cycle first prizes of $10,000 for a dress and $10,000 for a tux; runner-up and special prizes also offered.
deadline: The 2026 contest is complete. The 2027 entry dates and updated rules have not been published.
apply: Prior-cycle rules: create and wear original Duck Tape prom attire, then submit photos and written or video outfit details online. Attending prom is not required. Individual entry only; paid professional help is prohibited.
eligibility: Prior-cycle rules: high school students age 14+ residing in eligible US jurisdictions or Canada. Maryland, Colorado, Nebraska, North Dakota and Quebec are excluded. Previous finalists are ineligible.

name: Vantage West Scholarship
apply: The current official page says applications are closed. Check the official scholarship page for the next application link and required materials; the complete 2027 process is not published.
eligibility: 2027 college-location, membership and selection restrictions unverified.
notes: The official 2026 page says ten $5,000 awards and that applications are closed. A 2023 rules PDF restricted applicants to an Arizona postsecondary institution and required a credit-union member in good standing or member parent/guardian; those restrictions are historical and are not verified for 2027.

name: Courageous Persuaders Video Contest
apply: Create a safe-driving commercial of 30 seconds or less for a middle-school audience, upload it publicly and submit its link through the online entry form. Individuals or teams may enter; teams split awards. Finalists must supply consent forms for all participants.
eligibility: Grades 9-12, age 19 or under, attending school in the 48 contiguous states or D.C.

name: Community Impact Contest
value: $10,000 first / $5,000 second / $2,500 third; up to nine $500 honorable mentions
apply: Submit an implemented service project through the online portal with all required pitch, reflection and project documentation and participant consents. Qualifying activity must occur May 3,2026 through April 19,2027. Groups split awards.
eligibility: US citizens or legal residents ages 13-19 on January 1,2027, enrolled at eligible schools in the US, territories or American Armed Forces Schools abroad. Must be at least 13 when registering. Those graduating or receiving a GED before January 1,2027 and past top-prize winners are excluded.

name: E-waste Scholarship
apply: Complete the online application with a 140-character statement about e-waste. The current embedded form does not describe a finalist essay stage.
eligibility: High school students or current/entering college or graduate students, including homeschool. The program summary allows US citizens or legal residents and no age limit; embedded terms restrict registration below age 13 and use different residency wording.

name: All About Education Scholarship
value: Award amount unconfirmed: the official pages advertise $3,000, but the program’s embedded prize rules state $1,500.
apply: Submit the online application and an original English response of 250 words or less explaining how the scholarship would affect your life.
eligibility: Legal residents of the 50 US states orDC, age 14 orolder, currently enrolled or enrolling byfall 2032 in an accredited college, university or trade school. Sponsor employees and immediate family/household members are excluded.

name: Fifth Month Scholarship
apply: Submit an online application with an original English letter to the number five of 250 words or less.
eligibility: Legal residents of the 50 US states orDC. Embedded rules say age 13+ and accredited postsecondary enrollment byfall 2032; the summary says age 14+ andfall 2026. Confirm these conflicting terms with Unigo.

name: Altruism and All Good Deeds Scholarship
apply: Community-service essay, maximum 150 words.
eligibility: High school juniors or seniors, undergraduate or graduate students enrolled or planning part-time or full-time enrollment at an accredited US institution, including vocational/technical schools; GPA at least 2.5 on a 4.0 scale. Winners provide transcript and enrollment proof after selection.

name: We the Future Contest
apply: Submit the entry and permission form through the official portal with the materials required for your category. The essay is 500-700 words; other categories have their own length, video and project requirements. Parental consent is required for minors.
eligibility: US citizens or legal residents in grades 9-12, ages 14-19 at entry, attending eligible schools in the US, territories or Armed Forces schools abroad. Former winners may win at most twice and never twice in the same category.

name: Abbott and Fenner Scholarship
apply: Email an original 500-1,000-word educational, career and life-goals essay to scholarships@abbottandfenner.com, including your full name, mailing address and current school. AI-generated essays are prohibited.
eligibility: High school juniors and seniors, or students currently registered at an accredited postsecondary institution.
notes: Sponsor prohibits AI-generated submissions.

name: BigSun Athletics Scholarship
apply: Email an original 500-1,000-word essay on sports participation and its effects to athleticawards@bigsunathletics.com, with your name and current school. AI-generated essays are not accepted.
eligibility: Student-athletes who are high school seniors or attending a postsecondary institution, regardless of sport or participation capacity.

name: Digital Privacy Scholarship
apply: Complete the online application with a 140-character statement about digital privacy. The current embedded form does not describe a finalist essay stage.
eligibility: High school students or current/entering college or graduate students, including homeschool. The program summary allows US citizens or legal residents and no age limit; embedded terms restrict registration below age 13 and use different residency wording.

name: Gratitude Scholarship
apply: Complete the online application with one personal statement of 250 words or less about kindness, gratitude, or any topic of your choice. Responses are judged on content.
eligibility: US citizens or legal residents who are current high school students in grades 10-12 or college students, or plan to enter college within 12 months. Attend or plan to attend an accredited US postsecondary institution, including qualifying online programs. Demonstrate a commitment to education improving your life and your family or community. Need, grades and test scores are not considered.

name: Do-Over Scholarship
apply: Apply online with an original English response of up to 250 words describing a life event you would do over and why.
eligibility: Legal residents of the 50 US states or DC, age 14+. Embedded rules allow accredited postsecondary enrollment by fall 2032, but the summary says fall 2026. Confirm the enrollment requirement with Unigo.

name: Flavor of the Month Scholarship
apply: Apply online with an original English response of up to 250 words about which ice cream flavor reflects your personality and why.
eligibility: Legal residents of the 50 US states or DC, age 14 or older, currently enrolled or enrolling by fall 2032 at an accredited postsecondary institution. Sponsor employees and immediate family/household members are excluded.

name: Make Me Laugh Scholarship
apply: Apply online with an original English response of up to 250 words about a funny or embarrassing real or fictional incident.
eligibility: Legal residents of the 50 US states or DC, age 14 or older, currently enrolled or enrolling by fall 2032 at an accredited postsecondary institution. Sponsor employees and immediate family/household members are excluded.

name: Burger King Scholars
deadline: Opens October 15, 2026; closes December 15, 2026 or when 30,000 applications are received.
apply: Apply through the sponsor-linked Scholarship America portal when the 2027-2028 cycle opens. Prepare transcripts, activities and work history, household financial information, and employee details if applicable. The general and employee tracks have different requirements.
eligibility: Selection considers financial need, achievement and involvement. The detailed administrator rules still describe the 2026-2027 cohort, including general high school and employee/family tracks in the US, Puerto Rico, Guam and Canada. The 2027-2028 track-specific eligibility rules are not yet published.

name: Live Mas Scholarship
apply: Submit one original 30-second to 2-minute video or 250-500-word essay about your passion, intended impact and how you embody Live Más. Apply individually online during the application window.
eligibility: New applicants: legal residents of the 50 US states or DC located there, or dependent children of active-duty US military; ages 16-26; pursuing or planning accredited postsecondary education. Financial need is considered. Returning scholars have separate renewal rules.

name: In the Driver's Seat Scholarship
notes: Winners drawn at random from staff favorites; not purely merit.

name: BigFuture Scholarships (Class of 2027)
notes: Random drawing.

name: High School Senior Scholarship
notes: Random drawing.

name: Money Fit National Scholarship
notes: Random drawing.

name: High School Senior Scholarship
notes: Random drawing.

name: Sevens Legal High School Scholarship
apply: 1,000 words about revising a mistaken judgment; transcript required.
eligibility: US citizen or lawful permanent resident enrolled full-time as a senior at a US high school, with cumulative GPA at least 3.0. Sponsor employees and immediate family/household members are excluded.

name: Blue Planet Awareness Contest
apply: Submit original art, writing, film, performance or multimedia about environmental disinformation through the online platform, with an adult sponsor. Entries must be created during the 2026-27 academic year; AI-generated work is disqualified. Individuals or groups may enter; groups split awards.
eligibility: Ages 11-18 worldwide; must not have started college.
notes: Formerly Ocean Awareness.

provider: Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation
name: Science Without Borders Challenge
apply: Submit original handmade two-dimensional artwork on Navigate with Care, a finished-art photo and two progress photos through the online form. Teacher sponsorship is required; semifinalists mail the original. Digital and AI-generated artwork is ineligible.
eligibility: Primary/secondary or homeschool students worldwide ages 11-19; students age 10 may enter if turning 11 by March 1, 2027. College students are ineligible.

name: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
deadline: 2027 cycle not verified (2026 used March 15 and April 15)
apply: Complete the short pre-application first. Eligible applicants receive access to the full application with three recommendation letters submitted by references. A nonfamily adult familiar with the project serves as the lead reference.
eligibility: Ages 8-18 on April 15; permanent legal residents of the U.S./Canada. Significant student-led service with demonstrated impact.

provider: Jane Austen Society of North America
name: JASNA Essay Contest
deadline: The 2027 topic and rules will be published in November 2026; submissions open February 2027. The closing deadline is not published.
apply: Literary analysis.
eligibility: High school and homeschool students worldwide enrolled at that level during the contest year. College and graduate divisions have separate course-load rules. JASNA membership is not required.

name: Morris J. and Betty Kaplun Essay Contest
deadline: The 2025-2026 contest is closed. The next application dates have not been published.
apply: Essay on Jewish heritage/values.
eligibility: Grades 10-12 division; students worldwide of any religion.

name: EngineerTeen / EngineerGirl Writing Contest
apply: Submit an original short narrative and a matching 4-10-panel storyboard through the online form by February 1, 2027. Grade-specific narrative word limits are 800, 1,000, or 1,200 words; grades 7-12 need an APA reference list. A parent/guardian must consent.
eligibility: Students in grades 3-12, entering individually in one of the 2027 grade bands (3-4, 5-6, 7-9, 10-12). The work must be original; AI may help with research or brainstorming but may not write or create the final submission. The official 2027 page does not state a geographic restriction.
notes: Current 2027 prompt: train an AI robot to become safe, fair, and helpful in a real learning setting. Storyboard image must be PNG, JPG, or GIF and at most 3 MB. The general prize page lists $1,000/$750/$500, but does not label those amounts for 2027.

name: Kemper Human Rights Essay Contest
apply: Submit an English researched essay of up to 2,500 words excluding footnotes and bibliography by email as a Word attachment or by mail. Include school details, teacher certification and required student declarations; winners agree to a Zoom interview.
eligibility: High school students who are US citizens or residents enter the US contest. A separate international contest offers the same prize tiers to students who are citizens and residents of other countries.
notes: Generative AI prohibited even for brainstorming and outlining.

name: EnergyRates.ca Scholarship
apply: Submit an English or French essay of up to 500 words about the future of energy through the official online form, with name, email and address.
eligibility: Enrolled or planning to enroll at a U.S. or Canadian postsecondary institution within the next calendar year.

name: Online Journalist Scholarship
deadline: October 1 annually (2026 cycle not separately dated)
apply: Email a 500-word original news article on an interesting trend as a PDF to thehawkeronline@gmail.com, with name, school, study year, GPA and contact details.
eligibility: High school seniors or students in accredited part-time/full-time college courses; US citizens, permanent residents and international students are allowed. GPA at least 2.0. Students abroad at US-accredited universities may enter.

name: General Education and Mental Health Scholarship
deadline: November 30 and May 31 annually (year not specified)
apply: Submit an original essay addressing the addiction crisis, individual/societal consequences and remedies. A personal account or researched essay is allowed; 800-1,500 words is recommended, with no strict length limit.
eligibility: Full-time high school, university or college students in any major.

name: Sports Gear Swag Scholarship
apply: 500-word sports essay.
eligibility: Age 18+, a legal US resident or valid student-visa holder, and a high school senior accepted to a university or enrolled full-time in an accredited US undergraduate/graduate program. No GPA requirement.

name: Titan Haul & Honor Scholarship
apply: Essay on transportation, sustainability or planning.
eligibility: Age 18+, a legal US resident or valid student-visa holder, currently enrolled or accepted to a full-time accredited US undergraduate program, including accepted high school seniors.
notes: No military affiliation required.

name: Cybersecurity Innovation Scholarship
apply: Submit an original 300-word essay on email security, privacy or ransomware through the sponsor-linked Google application form.
eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at accredited US universities or high school seniors already accepted to a university program, with an interest in digital security, computer science or IT.
notes: No declared cybersecurity major required.

name: Safe Roads, Strong Futures Scholarship
apply: Submit a 500-700-word original road-safety essay as a Google Doc link, student ID, major and short bio through the online form using a school-designated email address. AI-written entries are rejected. Selected recipients consent to public recognition.
eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at accredited US universities or high school seniors accepted to a US university program. International students and family of company officers or the selection committee are excluded. Maintain continuous enrollment during the award period. The sponsor does not define permanent-resident eligibility.
notes: Permanent-resident treatment not defined.

name: Dream Builder Grant
apply: Short written responses or a 2-5-minute video.
eligibility: Accepted/enrolled U.S. undergraduate or trade student actively leading a real community initiative.
notes: Tuition grants go to the school.

name: Salt Lake Mailing Scholarship
apply: Email an original 800-1,200-word essay, name/contact/school/major/graduation details and proof of enrollment or acceptance to scholarship@saltlakemailing.com.
eligibility: High school seniors, undergraduate or graduate students enrolled or accepted at an accredited US college or university; GPA at least 3.0; all majors. Sponsor employees and their immediate family are excluded.
notes: No Utah residency requirement.

name: Design Your Space, Design Your Future
apply: Submit a 300-word design/environment essay as a Google Doc link through the sponsor-linked form, with a school-designated email address, contact number, major and short bio. AI-written responses are rejected. Selected recipients consent to public recognition.
eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at accredited US universities or high school seniors accepted to a university program, with an interest in creativity and improving environments. Architecture/design major is not required.

name: Craftsmanship & Design Excellence Scholarship
apply: 300-word essay about design/craftsmanship.
eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at accredited US universities or high school seniors accepted to a university program, demonstrating commitment to their field and an interest in design/craftsmanship.

name: Confidence Through Hair Loss Scholarship
apply: 500-word essay.
eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at accredited US universities or high school seniors accepted to a university program. Applicants may have medical hair-loss experience or pursue a career supporting affected people.

name: Love of Discovery Scholarship
apply: Submit an original 300-word essay about cultural immersion, a custom educational trip or travel challenges through the sponsor-linked application form.
eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled at accredited US universities or high school seniors accepted to a university program, with an interest in ongoing learning and exploring other cultures.

name: Personal Achievement / Injury Scholarship
apply: Submit an original essay of at least 500 words and resume through the official form. Explain the educational effect of a significant challenge, growth and future education. AI-generated essays are excluded.
eligibility: Students age 17+ enrolled at accredited US high schools as juniors/seniors planning college, or enrolled as college undergraduates, with a significant challenge affecting education.

name: Annual Video Contest
apply: Original 60-90-second AI-related video, branding and social-media steps.
eligibility: Current high school, college or university students worldwide; winners must prove academic status/enrollment.
notes: Judged first round, then YouTube likes: partly a popularity contest.

name: Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition
apply: Every participant must register and finish the free Blue Ocean Mini-Course. Submit one original English pitch video under five minutes through the pitch form with a YouTube link and #blueoceancompetition.
eligibility: Students worldwide enrolled in high school or equivalent pre-university study when registering; later graduation is allowed. Homeschooled students ages 14-18 may enter. Individual or team of up to five.
notes: Cash pitch competition; awards per winning entry.

name: Arthur M. & Berdena King Eagle Scout Contest
deadline: Chapter and state entry deadlines vary. February 15 is the annual national forwarding deadline, not the student application deadline. Specific 2027 local dates are not published.
apply: Application, four-generation ancestor chart and 500-word patriotic essay.
eligibility: Active registered Eagle Scouts who have not turned 19 during the January-December application year. Previous national first-place winners are excluded; an older-applicant exception may apply under the full rules.

name: SAR Youth Video Contest
value: Arizona state: $500 first, $250 second; national first prize currently listed as $1,750 on national page, versus $1,500 in older rules
deadline: Arizona: January 15 annually for chapter entries
apply: 3-5-minute Revolutionary-history video with at least three references.
eligibility: Grades 6-12; individual or group.
notes: National and state pages differ on first-place national value. The national rules PDF and Arizona page list $1,500, while the national program page lists $1,750. Do not rely on a national amount until current rules are issued.

name: Princeton Prize in Race Relations
apply: Online two-part application describing racial-equity work, supporting materials and an unrelated adult sponsor who witnessed the project; at-large review is available outside listed regions.
eligibility: U.S. grades 9-12 with actual racial-equity/understanding service. Open regardless of identity.
notes: Does not require attending Princeton.

name: Asian American Youth Scholarship
apply: A 350-500-word original essay, video introduction under one minute, one-page resume and unofficial transcript; selected finalists give an in-person five-minute presentation and two-minute Q&A. AI-generated materials are prohibited.
eligibility: High-school or undergraduate students with GPA 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent B average; currently study or reside in the U.S. Citizenship is not required. Mandatory in-person final; travel and lodging are not provided.
notes: Awards are paid directly to students for educational purposes. Travel and lodging are not provided.

name: Character Counts Scholarship
apply: Anyone, including the student, may nominate a student through Arizona Sports. Ten finalists are featured and invited to an award ceremony; judges choose the winner.
eligibility: Local Arizona high-school students ages 14-18 who demonstrate character, sportsmanship and community involvement.

name: Alisa's Angels Scholarship
value: $5,000 total for up to eight seniors: $2,500 in the first year, with the remainder in later years while in good standing; books and tuition paid directly to the school.
apply: Apply online through Arizona Community Foundation with a 750-word service essay, unofficial transcript through seventh semester and a reference from someone familiar with the service.
eligibility: The detailed scholarship page lists graduating Arizona seniors with GPA at least 2.75. The broader programs page and an official funding proposal also include Colorado Springs-area seniors, without clarifying whether they use the same GPA or application route. Service is primary; need, academic performance and activities are considered.
notes: The Arizona application rules are detailed, but Colorado Springs eligibility appears only in broader sponsor materials. Check the correct route and criteria before treating the Colorado pathway as open.

name: Presentation Crafting Scholarship
apply: Last published rules: original English presentation with 4-6 content slides, speaker notes and 3-6 MLA sources; submit Google Slides link, enrollment proof and required social-media screenshots by email.
eligibility: Current high-school, college or university students worldwide; winners must prove enrollment.

name: Custom Patches San Diego Scholarship
apply: The sponsor requires an original essay and says AI-generated or plagiarized work is ineligible, but provides no essay prompt, word limit, application form, or submission address on the official page.
eligibility: Applicants must be at least 18 and be U.S. legal residents or hold a valid student visa. The main rules allow those accepted to a full-time accredited U.S. college, university, or trade school, while the fine print says applicants must already be enrolled. High-school senior eligibility is therefore unclear.
notes: High-school senior route not confirmed.

name: George S. & Stella M. Knight Essay Contest
value: Arizona state first place: $500; national cash prize varies by year and is not confirmed for 2027
deadline: Arizona lists December 31 annually; chapter may be earlier
apply: Enter through a participating SAR chapter. Arizona rules require an original researched English essay of 800-1,200 words, title page, bibliography, biography and at least five references including three books.
eligibility: U.S. citizen or legal alien in grades 9-12 at a public, private, parochial or accredited home school; prior national first-place winners may not reenter.
notes: Arizona page lists an old $2,000 national first prize, while a later national rules PDF lists $6,000. The national handbook explicitly says national amounts are set annually. Enter through a local chapter before its own deadline.

name: Joseph S. Rumbaugh Historical Oration Contest
value: Arizona state $750 / $250 / $100; the state page lists national $8,000 / $5,000 / $3,000.
apply: Enter through a participating SAR chapter; prepare an original memorized 5-6-minute Revolutionary-history speech connecting the topic to America today, without notes or props. The national packet lists a manuscript, biographical sketch, photo, entry and release forms, plus a video for national competition. Follow the chapter and state submission instructions.
eligibility: Arizona high-school students in grades 9-12, including home schools, public, parochial and private schools.

name: Flinn Scholarship
value: Tuition, mandatory fees, housing and meals at ASU, NAU or the University of Arizona, plus study abroad and enrichment. Scholars must maintain 3.2 college GPA and participate in program activities.
deadline: Application October 13, 2026, 5 p.m.; recommendation/counselor materials October 27
apply: Online application with two essays and a short answer, one academic and one leadership/service recommendation, counselor transcript and school profile, and self-reported scores; semifinalist and finalist interviews follow.
eligibility: Arizona high-school seniors. U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident; Arizona residency for two full years before university entry. Published standards: 3.5 UW GPA, top 5% if ranked, ACT 26 or SAT 1230, and leadership (rare exceptions allowed).
notes: Applicants slightly below one or more academic standards can occasionally be selected; the foundation says such exceptions are rare.

name: College Scholarship Program
value: Up to $55,000 per year for up to four undergraduate years, after institutional aid; annual renewal considers GPA at least 3.0, need, conduct and progress.
apply: Apply through Common App by November 11, 2026 with short essays, financial and test information, self-reported grades and an unofficial transcript. Invite two academic teachers and a counselor for recommendations and the School Report. The FAQ says the counselor submits an official high-school transcript through Common App; an additional official copy may be requested from semifinalists.
eligibility: Seniors completing four years of high school in the U.S., a territory or U.S. military base and graduating spring 2027, intending an accredited four-year degree in fall 2027. At least 3.75 unweighted GPA, an SAT/ACT/AP/IB score and unmet financial need; family income ceiling $95,000. U.S. citizenship is not required.

name: Most Valuable Student Scholarship
value: 500 four-year awards: 20 of $30,000 total and 480 of $4,000 total.
apply: Online scholarship application, program code ElksMVS if requested. Top 20 finalists must attend the Chicago leadership weekend April 29-May 2, 2027 to receive $30,000.
eligibility: Current U.S. citizen high-school seniors, not graduates; permanent residents do not qualify. No Elks family relationship required. Scholarship, leadership and need are considered. Award requires full-time enrollment in an accredited U.S. four-year undergraduate degree program.

name: Squire; A.W. Smith; Wolf scholarships
value: Squire: full tuition (eligible disciplines incl. management/accountancy and sciences). A.W. Smith: full tuition (engineering/physical science/math). Wolf: tuition, room, board, fees and books.
deadline: Admission deadline varies by round; competition application February 15 (year not stated on scholarship page).
apply: Apply to Case Western Reserve by the admission deadline, then complete a separate scholarship competition application with additional information and an essay response for each award sought.
eligibility: First-year applicants; international students may enter unless otherwise noted. Squire covers specified arts, humanities, management, accountancy and sciences; Smith requires a successful hands-on science/engineering project and relevant intended field; Wolf prioritizes character and leadership. Students already eligible for full-tuition CWRU benefits cannot enter.
notes: Squire, A.W. Smith, and Wolf are three separate competitions with different intended fields and selection criteria. The university does not publish their individual essay prompts on the overview page.

name: A.B. Duke and Duke-administered merit
value: Tuition, mandatory fees, room and board for four years of full-time undergraduate study.
deadline: Duke 2026-27 admission: Early Decision November 2, 2026; Regular Decision January 4, 2027. No separate Duke-administered merit application.
apply: Duke admission application provides initial consideration, with spring finalist interviews; no separate application for Duke-administered awards.
eligibility: Incoming first-year Duke applicants are considered through admission. A.B. Duke recognizes intellectual accomplishment; Alumni Endowed requires a Duke alumni parent/grandparent and some financial need; B.N. name: Nemerov Writing Scholars; Olin Distinguished Scholars
value: Nemerov Writing Scholars: up to ten $3,000 annual awards. Olin Distinguished Scholars: up to ten full-tuition scholarships. Both renewable up to four years with satisfactory degree progress.
deadline: Nemerov: apply to Arts & Sciences by December 16, 2026 for priority, then submit writing samples by January 4, 2027. Olin: admission application by January 4, 2027; no separate scholarship form.
apply: Nemerov: select College of Arts & Sciences and upload two creative-writing samples, preferably different genres, in WashU Pathway. Olin: select Olin Business School on the admission application; eligible applicants are automatically considered.
eligibility: Nemerov is for entering Arts & Sciences students with exceptional creative-writing potential who pursue a writing minor. Olin Distinguished Scholars is for entering Olin Business School applicants; selection considers character, academics, leadership, community service and promise in business.
notes: These are two distinct school scholarships with separate routes and values; the stated dates apply to fall 2027 entry.
